summary: Minimal, correct fix: sets self.pk = None after collector.delete() in Model.delete(), directly resolving the reported issue where deleting an instance with no dependent objects (fast-delete path) left the PK on the in-memory instance. Placement after collector.delete() ensures post_delete signal receivers still see the original pk, consistent with existing behavior for cascade-deleted related objects.

issues.description: Only clears pk on the instance calling delete(); does not affect other code paths (e.g. QuerySet.delete() or direct Collector.delete() use) which have their own separate pk-clearing logic, but that is outside the scope of this specific issue.
